purpose: Descriptive, after v7s's record (post hoc; not part of v7s's deposited conditions), run once on the work PC: whether the page's times in Firefox 160 sit on a step of about 15.625 ms (1/64 s), for the time the event carries (event.timeStamp, page.ndjson's t_ms) and for the time the handler ran (performance.now(), h_ms), beside Chrome's page on the same PC. It answers why v7s's predictions 4 (second half) and 5 (first half) failed: Firefox's page path_sd was 5.7 to 7.4 ms at the known gaps of 18 to 200 ms, and D1 flipped none of F_M2's page sessions.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-20 after v7s's record (SHA-256 9ff1d37a..., read on the Mac: Firefox's page gaps on the 1 ms grid in every capture; at the known gaps of 1 to 5 ms 68 to 94% of the gaps dropped as equal times and the median 1 to 5 ms short of the plan; path_sd 5.7 to 7.4 ms at 18 to 200 ms; the smoke's first page times 4280, 4280, 4280, 4296, 4296) and after the researcher's decision 2 of .steering/20261120-v9-returns. Neither h_ms in any capture nor the distribution of the page gaps beyond v7s's record has been seen. Code: works/prototype_v7t.py, committed with this file; it imports v7's analysis code at a6fa5ca and v7s's at 5508490 unchanged and checks both byte for byte before reading anything. Amended before any value after the code review (Claude and Codex, 2026-11-20): a press with an h_ms that is not a finite number stops the run; the code checks the base commits and v7s's conditions against this file; the hook layer's gaps of every machine capture are described beside the page's (not read); the Chrome comparison's limit is written below; the denominator of the share of captures and the readings' wording are made exact; tests run v7s's own loaders on fake folders and call main.
captures: v7s's captures as v7s's analysis reads them (its runlogs and load_item): the known gaps F_K (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 18, 50, 100, 200 ms), K_chrome (0, 1, 2, 3, 5), F_K_nohook and K_chrome_nohook (0, 1, 2, 3, 5); the series MC1, MC2, MC3, MC5, F_M0, F_M2_8B, F_M2_14B and F_H1; and v7's P_idle (5, 18, 50, 100, 200 ms, Chrome) as v7's load_all reads it. The presses of each page are those v7's read_page counts (key downs of a counted kind, repeats left out, in capture order); the run stops if the presses read here give other t_ms than read_page's. A series' items are those of v7s's runlogs (every item v7s's plan made is in them, including no_plan and failed ones, which are counted as not captured).
count: For each known-gap capture and each of t_ms and h_ms: the gaps in capture order with nothing dropped; the number of gaps; the share equal to zero (within 1e-6 ms); the share on the 1 ms grid; the share of the positive gaps on the step (within tolerance_ms of k * step_ms, k >= 1); the smallest positive gap; the five most frequent positive gaps in 0.1 ms bins with their shares; v7s's path_measures (median minus planned, raw_sd, path_sd after v6's cleaning, dropped share). Also the lag h_ms minus t_ms per press (min, 5th to 95th percentiles, max). For each series: over its captured items, the quantiles of the per-capture shares (machine series with min and max; F_H1 without, as v7's summary for persons, and nothing but the count below 5), the share of captures with at least on_step_at_least of their positive gaps on the step (not given below 5 captures), and the quantiles of the per-capture median lag. No kind, key, text, plan or per-person value is written. For each machine capture with a hook layer, the same gap measures of the hook's times (QPC), as a description beside the page's: the hook's step, if any, shows whether the presses were sent on a step; not read. The share of captures on the step counts over the captures that have at least one positive gap on that side; a capture with none is left out of it.

reading.rule: From the long known gaps (18, 50, 100, 200 ms, hook installed), per side, the share of positive gaps on the step in each of the four captures. Firefox's event time (F_K, t_ms), Firefox's handler time (F_K, h_ms), Chrome's event time (v7's P_idle, t_ms): 'on the step' if all four shares are at least on_step_at_least; 'not on the step' if all four are at most off_step_at_most; else, or if one is missing, 'not decided'. where_in_firefox: 'the event's time only' if Firefox's event time is 'on the step' and its handler time is 'not on the step'; 'the delivery too' if both are 'on the step'; else 'not decided'. pc_wide: 'no' if Firefox's event time is 'on the step' and Chrome's is 'not on the step'; else 'not decided' (a step in Chrome too would not by itself show a PC-wide cause, so 'yes' is not read).
reading.why: With a step of 1/64 s and integer times, a gap of k steps reads as 15 or 16, 31 or 32, 46 or 47, 62 or 63 ms; a tolerance of 1 ms takes them all. The planned gaps 18, 50, 100 and 200 ms lie 2.4, 3.1, 6.25 and 3.1 ms from the nearest multiple, outside the tolerance, so a page that keeps the planned gaps reads 'not on the step'. Gaps spread evenly would fall on the step about 2 * 1.0 / 15.625 = 0.13 of the time.

limits: Post hoc and descriptive: it does not change v7s's verdict, cells or predictions, which stay as read. One PC, one Firefox version (160.0.1.0), Windows' timer not measured. The series' shares mix gaps of all sizes and are given as description, not read. A step found here names where the time is coarse (the event's time or the delivery), not why. Chrome's long known gaps are v7's P_idle, captured in v7's run on the same PC days before v7s's F_K, not beside them: Windows' timer resolution can change with what each process asks for, so pc_wide 'no' says that on this PC a page in Chrome did not show the step when v7 ran, not that the two browsers were compared at one time.
record: results/prototype_v7t/record.json: known_gaps, series, readings, provenance (HEAD, dirty, conditions and code SHA-256). Refuses to overwrite.
